title: Un-commit, keep the work
brief:
The last commit ("add marketing page") went in too early and with the wrong story. The WORK is good; the COMMIT is wrong. You want to un-commit it and recommit it properly.

`git reset` moves the branch pointer back. Its three modes decide what happens to the other two trees: `--hard` also rewrites the index and the workdir (the work is GONE), `--mixed` resets the index but keeps your files, and `--soft` keeps index and files exactly as they are.

You want the page to stay staged for an instant recommit. That is `--soft`. Then commit again with the right message: "add landing page".

goals.label: The recommit tells the right story

hints: git reset --soft HEAD~1 moves main back one commit but leaves page.txt staged.
--hard would have deleted page.txt from disk. --mixed would have kept the file but unstaged it. --soft keeps the stage, which is why it is one commit command away from done.
